title: Quantitative Aspects of Chemical Change

standard_text: The mole and molar mass; calculations with n = m/M and n = N/Nₐ; concentration (c = n/V); percentage composition, empirical and molecular formulae; simple stoichiometric calculations. (summary of the senior secondary Chemistry curriculum, SSS 2; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 Chemistry worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): the mole and Avogadro's number, molar mass and conversions, concentration, percentage composition and empirical formulae and stoichiometry. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

The mole is the SI unit for amount of substance. One mole of any substance contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number). The molar mass M (g·mol⁻¹) is the mass of one mole and is found from the periodic table.

Use n = m/M to change mass to moles, and c = n/V (V in dm³) for solutions. The balanced equation gives the mole ratio of reactants and products. The empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.

Example

How many moles are in 36 g of water (M = 18 g·mol⁻¹)?

n = m/M

Answer: 2 mol

Example

0.5 mol NaCl in 0.25 dm³. Concentration?

c = n/V

Answer: 2 mol·dm⁻³

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to change cm³ to dm³.
  • Using the mass ratio instead of the mole ratio.
  • Confusing molar mass with mass.

faq.q: What is the molar mass of CO₂?
What is the difference between an empirical and a molecular formula?
faq.a: The empirical formula gives the simplest ratio (CH₂O); the molecular formula gives the actual numbers of atoms (C₆H₁₂O₆).

items.q: What is the molar mass of water?
What is the SI unit of the amount of substance?
Calculate the mass of 0.20 mol of C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>.
A sample has 2.41 × 10<sup>24</sup> particles of calcium carbonate (CaCO<sub>3</sub>). How many moles is that?
How many moles of atoms in total are in 1 mol of sulfuric acid (H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 7 atoms, so 1 × 7 = 7 mol.

items.q: How many moles of atoms in total are in 3 mol of hydrogen chloride (HCl)?
items.e: Each formula has 2 atoms, so 3 × 2 = 6 mol.

items.q: How many moles of atoms in total are in 1 mol of water (H<sub>2</sub>O)?
items.e: Each formula has 3 atoms, so 1 × 3 = 3 mol.

items.q: How many moles of O atoms are in 0.5 mol of sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 3 O, so 0.5 × 3 = 1.5 mol.

items.q: Which law says a compound always contains the same elements in the same proportion by mass?
c: the law of conservation of mass

items.q: How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 4 mol of propane (C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>)?
How many moles of atoms in total are in 4 mol of sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 6 atoms, so 4 × 6 = 24 mol.

items.q: How many molecules or formula units are in 25.0 g of CaCl<sub>2</sub>? (N<sub>A</sub> = 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> mol⁻¹)
A sample has 1.20 × 10<sup>24</sup> particles of magnesium chloride (MgCl<sub>2</sub>). How many moles is that?
Calculate the mass of 0.15 mol of C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>.
Which is a homogeneous mixture?
items.e: Its composition is the same throughout.

items.q: How many moles of C atoms are in 0.5 mol of sucrose (C<sub>12</sub>H<sub>22</sub>O<sub>11</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 12 C, so 0.5 × 12 = 6 mol.

items.q: Calculate the mass of 0.10 mol of NaCl.
A sample has 6.02 × 10<sup>24</sup> particles of ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>). How many moles is that?
What is a pure substance?
c: a substance with a fixed composition, an element or a compound
items.e: Its properties are the same throughout.

items.q: How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 4 mol of aluminium oxide (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>)?
What is the mass of 2.5 mol of iron(III) oxide (Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>)? (Molar mass = 160 g/mol)

How many moles are in 270 g of glucose (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>)? (Molar mass = 180 g/mol)

18.0 g of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is dissolved in 200 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 180 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0.100 ÷ 0.200 = 0.500 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: 15.0 g of Na₂CO₃ is dissolved in water to make 100 mL of solution. What is the molarity? (molar mass 106 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Moles = 15.0 ÷ 106 = 0.142 mol; M = moles ÷ volume in L = 0.142 ÷ 0.100 = 1.42 mol dm⁻³.

items.q: 0.4 mol of hydrochloric acid is dissolved to make 200 cm³ of solution. What is its concentration?
A solution of sodium chloride has a concentration of 2 mol/dm³. What is its concentration in g/dm³? (Mr = 58.5)
How many moles of hydrochloric acid are in 250 cm³ of a 0.25 mol/dm³ solution?
What volume of 0.2 mol/dm³ sodium chloride contains 0.04 mol?
16.0 g of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) is dissolved in 250 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 342 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0.0468 ÷ 0.250 = 0.187 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: 9.00 g of CaCl₂ is dissolved in water to make 100 mL of solution. What is the molarity? (molar mass 111 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Moles = 9.00 ÷ 111 = 0.0811 mol; M = moles ÷ volume in L = 0.0811 ÷ 0.100 = 0.811 mol dm⁻³.

items.q: What volume of 2 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide contains 0.2 mol?
What volume of 0.1 mol/dm³ sodium chloride contains 0.005 mol?
9.50 g of KOH is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution. What is the molarity? (molar mass 56 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Moles = 9.50 ÷ 56 = 0.170 mol; M = moles ÷ volume in L = 0.170 ÷ 0.500 = 0.339 mol dm⁻³.

items.q: 20.0 g of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) is dissolved in 250 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 342 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0.0585 ÷ 0.250 = 0.234 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: 27 g of KCl is dissolved in 250 g of water. What is the mass percentage of the solute?
items.e: Mass % = mass of solute ÷ mass of solution × 100 = 27 ÷ 277 × 100 = 9.75%.

items.q: 34.0 g of Na₂CO₃ is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution. What is the molarity? (molar mass 106 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Moles = 34.0 ÷ 106 = 0.321 mol; M = moles ÷ volume in L = 0.321 ÷ 0.500 = 0.642 mol dm⁻³.

items.q: How many moles of copper(II) sulfate are in 250 cm³ of a 0.5 mol/dm³ solution?
16.5 g of KCl is dissolved in water to make 200 mL of solution. What is the molarity? (molar mass 74.5 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Moles = 16.5 ÷ 74.5 = 0.221 mol; M = moles ÷ volume in L = 0.221 ÷ 0.200 = 1.11 mol dm⁻³.

items.q: 0.25 mol of sodium hydroxide is dissolved to make 250 cm³ of solution. What is its concentration?
21.0 g of KOH is dissolved in 250 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 56 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0.375 ÷ 0.250 = 1.50 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: 15.5 g of KOH is dissolved in 100 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 56 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0.277 ÷ 0.100 = 2.77 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: 13.5 g of CaCl₂ is dissolved in 100 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 111 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0.122 ÷ 0.100 = 1.22 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: What percent of the mass of propane (C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>) is C? (H = 1, C = 12; molar mass = 44 g/mol)
A compound contains C 82.8%, H 17.2% by mass. What is its empirical formula?
items.e: Divide each % by A<sub>r</sub>, then divide by the smallest: C 6.90, H 17.2.

items.q: A compound contains 12 g of C, 3 g of H. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: CH₃.

items.q: What percent of the mass of hydrogen chloride (HCl) is H? (H = 1, Cl = 35.5; molar mass = 36.5 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of water (H<sub>2</sub>O) is O? (H = 1, O = 16; molar mass = 18 g/mol)
Who stated the law of conservation of mass?
items.e: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction.

items.q: Calculate the molar mass (in g mol⁻¹) of NaHCO<sub>3</sub>.
What percent of the mass of methane (CH<sub>4</sub>) is H? (H = 1, C = 12; molar mass = 16 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>) is N? (H = 1, N = 14; molar mass = 17 g/mol)
Calculate the molar mass (in g mol⁻¹) of CuSO<sub>4</sub>.
What percent of the mass of carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>) is C? (C = 12, O = 16; molar mass = 44 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>) is Na? (C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23; molar mass = 106 g/mol)
A compound contains 1.2 g of C, 0.2 g of H. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: CH₂.

items.q: What percent of the mass of methane (CH<sub>4</sub>) is C? (H = 1, C = 12; molar mass = 16 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of iron(III) oxide (Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) is O? (O = 16, Fe = 56; molar mass = 160 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of calcium carbonate (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) is C? (C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40; molar mass = 100 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of glucose (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>) is O? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16; molar mass = 180 g/mol)
A compound contains 92.3% C, 7.69% H by mass. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: CH.

items.q: A compound contains 4.6 g of Na, 3.2 g of S, 6.4 g of O. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: Na = 23, S = 32, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: Na₂SO₄.

items.q: A compound contains Fe 69.9%, O 30.1% by mass. What is its empirical formula?
items.e: Divide each % by A<sub>r</sub>, then divide by the smallest: Fe 1.25, O 1.88.

items.q: When aluminium reacts with acid: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl<sub>3</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of AlCl<sub>3</sub> to HCl?
When iron rusts: 4Fe + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. How many moles of Fe are needed to make 0.5 mol of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: 0.5 mol Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> × (4 mol Fe ÷ 2 mol Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) = 1 mol.

items.q: When ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. What mass of H<sub>2</sub> is needed to make 68 g of NH<sub>3</sub>? (NH<sub>3</sub> = 17 g/mol, H<sub>2</sub> = 2 g/mol)

When an acid is neutralised: H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + 2NaOH → Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O. What mass of H<sub>2</sub>O form from 98 g of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>? (H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> = 98 g/mol, H<sub>2</sub>O = 18 g/mol)
When ethane burns: 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> + 7O<sub>2</sub> → 4CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. How many moles of O<sub>2</sub> react with 8 mol of C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>?
items.e: 8 mol C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> × (7 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 2 mol C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>) = 28 mol.

items.q: When nitrogen oxide forms in an engine: N<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2NO. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to NO?

When aluminium reacts with oxygen: 4Al + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. What mass of Al is needed to make 51 g of Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>? (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> = 102 g/mol, Al = 27 g/mol)
When aluminium reacts with acid: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl<sub>3</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>. How many moles of H<sub>2</sub> form from 1 mol of Al?
items.e: 1 mol Al × (3 mol H<sub>2</sub> ÷ 2 mol Al) = 1.5 mol.

items.q: When iron is made in a blast furnace: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>. How many moles of CO<sub>2</sub> form along with 3 mol of Fe?
items.e: 3 mol Fe × (3 mol CO<sub>2</sub> ÷ 2 mol Fe) = 4.5 mol.

items.q: When aluminium reacts with oxygen: 4Al + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. How many moles of O<sub>2</sub> are needed to make 0.5 mol of Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: 0.5 mol Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> × (3 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 2 mol Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) = 0.75 mol.

items.q: When potassium chlorate decomposes: 2KClO<sub>3</sub> → 2KCl + 3O<sub>2</sub>. What mass of O<sub>2</sub> form along with 7.45 g of KCl? (KCl = 74.5 g/mol, O<sub>2</sub> = 32 g/mol)
When aluminium reacts with oxygen: 4Al + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. How many moles of O<sub>2</sub> are needed to make 10 mol of Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: 10 mol Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> × (3 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 2 mol Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>) = 15 mol.

items.q: When hydrogen burns in oxygen: 2H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to H<sub>2</sub>O?
When nitrogen oxide forms in an engine: N<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2NO. What is the mole ratio of NO to O<sub>2</sub>?
When hydrogen peroxide decomposes: 2H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O + O<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>?

When methane burns: CH<sub>4</sub> + 2O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O. What mass of CO<sub>2</sub> form from 8 g of O<sub>2</sub>? (O<sub>2</sub> = 32 g/mol, CO<sub>2</sub> = 44 g/mol)
When ethane burns: 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> + 7O<sub>2</sub> → 4CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. How many moles of H<sub>2</sub>O form along with 3 mol of CO<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: 3 mol CO<sub>2</sub> × (6 mol H<sub>2</sub>O ÷ 4 mol CO<sub>2</sub>) = 4.5 mol.

items.q: When glucose is used in respiration: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> → 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. What mass of CO<sub>2</sub> form from 540 g of C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>? (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> = 180 g/mol, CO<sub>2</sub> = 44 g/mol)
When ethane burns: 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> + 7O<sub>2</sub> → 4CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. How many moles of H<sub>2</sub>O form from 6 mol of C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>?
items.e: 6 mol C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> × (6 mol H<sub>2</sub>O ÷ 2 mol C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>) = 18 mol.

items.q: When ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. What mass of H<sub>2</sub> is needed to make 17 g of NH<sub>3</sub>? (NH<sub>3</sub> = 17 g/mol, H<sub>2</sub> = 2 g/mol)
